description: 631-19-002 Upgrade Steam Distribution System Phase 2 Industry Day Recap Understand Challenges for construction regarding this project from a contractor s perspective. Is there any ability to alter phasing? VA Response: In-short, yes. As a result of your inquiries the project team is proposing phasing to turn over both basement and first floor wings coordinate well in advance to close, relocate, or adjust clinical operations for a fixed period. This includes a lengthy shut down of the canteen in summer months. This will allow more day shift work, more sustained/efficient construction avoiding nightly restoration. With careful planning and temporary heat provision plans by contractor this could also permit work during heating season. The solicitation will contain an updated phasing supplement by wings with permissible down time that shall supersede any specification or drawing phasing plans. We anticipate evaluating proposals with at least 1 factor demonstrating a contractor s utilization of these updates to indicate their time and cost savings relative to off-hours work. This supplement will also include operation constraints such as audiology and pharmacy where noisy work and infection control issues will push to off hours work. When is this project going to be solicited? VA Response: The intention is for this to be solicited late quarter three or quarter four. This presents an excellent opportunity for the awardee to utilize the winter of 26/27 to procure materials, complete admin and detailed coordination drawings for building 1, while utilizing immediately available work in buildings 15 and 16 to establish team dynamics, rhythm, and process to build steam. Are there any specific needs of the facility? Can a contractor utilize temporary heaters? Can a contractor bring in an engineering team to help assist? VA Response: VA would be willing to review these proposed methods. Again, the expectation is for a best value solicitation. The VA is highly motivated to complete this critical infrastructure. We will gladly review RFIs and evaluate tradeoffs. Topics so far we would happy to entertain: Value engineering proposal to change any load to hydronic. Rough sizing calcs demonstrating heating loads are satisfied Advantages: Copper/pluming work vs schedule 80 pipe welding. Significant pipe size reduction in mains, elimination of traps and maintenance costs long term, elimination of gravity dependent pathways. Elimination of smaller condensate pumps such as PTOT, customer care suite, canteen, mech room (still one in sub-basement), elimination of canteen CP by Walk-in. Savings proposals based on phasing supplement and temp heating to allow more winter work. Proposal to include products such as dryers and low maintenance sustainment. Any proposals increasing serviceable and low maintenance sustainment or energy rebate alternative ideas could be considered under best value Rathert than working above drop ceilings propose potential ceiling replacements if phasing supplement turns over. E.G: Canteen just demo drop ceiling to save demo and construction efforts, especially with ACM. Establish new IAW specifications. Propose net savings/cost trade off Canteen store drop ceiling replace Section of hallway leading to canteen, proposed elimination with cosmetic clean up Has the VA confirmed the pipe sizing and gravity of the system? VA Response: The VA has performed a qualitative review and directed drawing updates based on sizing. It is believed the current new work plan is largely oversized without being excessive, but to our knowledge no quantitative analysis exists. Is there any consideration to move away from the non-destructive testing? There are potential pitfalls in utilizing this method. VA Response: VA will look at this and review the methods. The current thought process is to establish minimal surveillance or critical areas where NDT including radiation exclusion radius/sphere will be performed off hours. This will likely be a hybrid between the standard specification and more than B31.1 would typically require. It could also include requirement to document process for items like socket weld (e.g. construction photo showing insertion scribe and back off . Has the VA looked at the potential use of swing spaces? Other VA s have utilized this approach to allow large areas to be vacated in an effort to provide uninterrupted work. VA Response: The utilization of swing spaces is being explored. VA will provide an updated phasing supplement with the solicitation. Is there the ability block off more rooms at a time to avoid the need to restore rooms each day? VA Response: This could be considered. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. Can the Canteen be down for an extended period of time? VA Response: VA is looking into potentially shutting this down for a period of time to allow efficient work. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. How would the VA handle unforeseen asbestos? Is there the ability to utilize a unit price? VA Response: This could be a potential line item for the solicitation. Has the VA looked at reducing the requirement for a degreed engineer for the MEP Coordinator, or all other disciplines? VA Response: VA will take a look at the requirements, but having a qualified MEP Coordinator on this specific job is the intention. Is there the ability for an administrative NTP to be issued? This would allow for more thorough site investigations and planning. It appears that in order to do a proper investigation and coordination drawings the period would need to be longer than the one-hundred and twenty (120) days in the specifications. VA Response: VA will take this under consideration. The intention is that the project will be solicited soon with the target of awarding the project at the beginning of Quarter 1. Historically this period is not well utilized by prime contractors. However, an evaluation factor with major milestones schedule and Proposed Period of Performance would be likely for this project resulting in the intent of this question and maximum flexibility for the prime contractor. The VA would greatly value any commitment that documents the bulk of the administrative data and planning before mobilizing; we believe this is best value for the government and the prime contractor. Understand the major cost drivers. Could a mega-press be used on lower PSI distributions? This has the potential to lower the costs as the need for welders would be minimized VA Response: VA is willing to entertain alternative methods so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications. This would need to be an RFI, there are issues when schedule 80 is called for. If allowed it will likely have size limitations for condensate and smaller for LP steam. Could condensers be stainless steel? They save on weight and performance is similar to what is in the specifications. VA Response: VA would be willing to entertain alternative methods so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications. Deviations or value engineering proposals deviating to above and beyond such as stainless steel can be considered pre award depending on solicitation details What if any value engineering ideas should be considered. Would the VA consider adding moisture separators into the project? Although they are not included adding them in would allow for extended warranties on equipment, there are additional costs associated with adding them in. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The scope of this project is to replace all data infrastructure across the Gainesville VAMC and to build a new data center to support that upgraded system. The data center building will be one story, and the footprint will be approximately 3,931 SF at the location of temporary trailer 11, which will be demolished as part of this project. The primary space within the building is the 1,177 SF Data Center Room. Supporting spaces include Unpacking/Packing/Staging, Entrance Room, and Storage. Mechanical, Electrical, and HVAC spaces. Additionally, a new generator will be housed in a separate Generator Room. Also, this project will be removing all existing equipment and cabling affiliated with the telecom rooms in all campus buildings. There are 59 telecom rooms that may require architectural work. Some rooms are existing TRs being reused, but most are new rooms being redesigned for the telecom equipment. In rare cases telecom enclosures are recommended and/or exceptions will be required. The entire campus will be occupied while work occurs. Contractor will have to coordinate room closures and shutdowns with the COR. Most rooms on campus will be affected. Some off-hour work is anticipated for more critical spaces. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as an Invitation for Bids (IFB) conducted in accordance with FAR part 14 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in mid to late July 2026, with an estimated late September 2026 award. The period of performance is approximately 921 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000 and $50,000,000 (although the middle of this range is more relevant). This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Shawn.Tavernia@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

description: Purpose: This is a Sources Sought. The Space Systems Command (SSC) located at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is seeking information in the form of Statements of Capabilities (SOC) from interested parties in support of the SSC, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power Directorate requirement for the Counter Communications System (CCS) Meadowlands as described below. The Government is conducting market research to inform its Acquisition Strategy. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources that can meet CFC/MD3�s requirement. The Government reserves the right to set this acquisition, or portions thereof, aside for small business � to include socially and economically disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, or woman-owned businesses. The Government is seeking contractors interested in and capable of providing all technical and logistical effort required to design, develop, and deliver capabilities to support the CCS Meadowlands system. Background and Description: Scope: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems. Period and Place of Performance: It is envisioned that the period of performance will be approximately 12 months in duration. The Government is working through the details to determine when the contract will start. The place of performance is flexible to allow contractor to provide an optimized solution. Background: CCS System: CCS is a ground-based counter satellite communications (SATCOM) system specifically designed to reversibly deny, disrupt, and degrade adversarial SATCOM. The basic CCS concept is to provide a flexible, modular, scalable, rapidly deployable system with a key set of signal processing/generation (SP) capabilities, selected counter SATCOM missions, and a robust transmit capability. Its architecture will be designed to host core capabilities and/or other more sophisticated �plug and play� type modules to address the ever-increasing number of technologies and assets available to our adversaries. The latest CCS Meadowlands will have upgraded capabilities compared to the existing CCS 10.2 Systems. The future CCS Meadowlands fleet will be composed of at least 32 systems. Meadowlands is a transportable SATCOM system composed of modular Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) / Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring and generation equipment. The design incorporates multi-band antennas and equipment in transit cases. The frequency conversion system (FCS) that handles RF signals between the shelter transit cases to the antenna uses a proprietary photonics system. The system can be transported by C-130 or larger aircraft and by ground transport over improved or semi-improved roads. The system will be designed for operations by trained operators in US-controlled facilities world-wide, and in the Developmental Support Facility (DSF). The Meadowlands �Base Design� system meets current A-spec requirements. All systems have same Transit Case and Antenna configuration/capability. The Meadowlands base design system is comprised of the following major capabilities: Three independent, bidirectional antenna polarization paths Native Support for a single Large Multiband Antenna (LMA) Bands Supported: UHF, L, C, Ku, Ka Two separate independently controlled antenna polarization paths Simultaneous dual polarization operation Receive-only operation if desired Supports Base, and unique network specific missions Native Support for a single 1.2m Antenna Antenna Supports L-Band only The system can operate in three antenna Polarization Paths � Each Polarization Path Contains an Uplink & Downlink RF Interface. The system is capable of simultaneously operating/controlling up to three antennas and associated components utilizing three polarization paths. The Meadowlands system utilizes Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Ethernet, TCP & UDP/IP Standard interfaces for network communications (Data, Command, Control & Status) between Transit case assemblies, Antennas and the Software Server The Base System Configuration is composed of: 4 System Transit Cases in Shelter (Mission Control & Timing (MCT) Subsystem, Advanced Signal Processor (ASP) Subsystem, Shelter Photonics Unit (SPU1), SPU2) 1 Antenna Transit Case in Shelter for 1.2m Antenna (1.2m Transit Case) 1 Transit Case for Secure External Network Operations (Remote Ops Transit Case) � Contains Firewall & Encryption 2 Transit Cases outside by LMA antenna (Antenna Photonics Unit (APU)2 & APU2) APU Transit Cases The system can operate in the UHF, L, C, Ku, and KA RF Bands for Transmit and Receive via Frequency Conversion System (FCS) The production of the CCS Meadowlands units has been accomplished as part of a Pre-Planned Product Improvement effort. The program utilizes equipment from the CCS Block 10.2 systems as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) including the LMA Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, High Powered Amplifiers (HPAs), Dummy Loads); the 1.2m Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, HPAs, Dummy Loads), Power Distribution Units (PDUs) (in transit cases) and also external PDUs, Environmental Control Units (ECUs), Tent, and a Power Management Unit (PMU) Requirements: The market research obtained from this request for information will be used to support a Government decision on the award of additional CCS Meadowlands systems between seven and up to an additional 24 systems. The intent for any future systems to follow the same design and functionality as the existing Meadowlands systems for efficiency in sustainment, training and and maintenance for the operational units. description: The United States Government (USG), Space Systems Command (SSC), and Tactical SATCOM Division (SSC/TX), in coordination with the Directorate of Contracting (SSC/CGK), is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of performing System Integrator (SI) functions or activities in support of the Enterprise Management & Control (EM&C) program. If interested in pursuing this opportunity, please submit a video to P1SM no later than end of October 2026 to allow time for your submission to be assessed in accordance with the competitive procedures of P1SM. The anticipated period of performance for the resultant award will consist of a 12?month base period and four 12?month option periods. The SI is responsible for planning, executing, and validating integrations between the EM&C platform and external programs/data repositories, including the Joint Management Tool (JMT), Unified Data Library (UDL), EMS Beskar, Blitzar, Protected and Tactical Systems (PATS) Mission Management System, and external commercial/government off-the-shelf software (COTS/GOTS). The SI contractor will not author core application code or dictate enterprise reference architecture. Core application code is developed by designated Development Contractors (DEV), while the architectural roadmap and governance are established by System Engineering & Integration Contractors (SE&I). The SI operates as the technical integrator and operational execution engine thereby, driving Program Increment (PI) planning, deployment automation, release orchestration, and enterprise-level test and evaluation (T&E). The ECB envisages launching a dynamic purchasing system with a duration of initially two years, extendable at the ECB's option by another two years (total duration up to four years).

title: Heavy Equipment Rental Services
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors capable of providing heavy equipment rental services to support laboratory operations at INL facilities in Idaho Falls and at Site locations west of Idaho Falls. BACKGROUND INL utilizes outside vendors to obtain equipment that is unavailable through the Central Facilities Area (CFA) equipment pool or required for specialized tasks. Timely access to safe, compliant, and well-maintained equipment is essential to maintaining project schedules and mitigating risk. Heavy equipment rentals enable BEA to meet operational needs without long-term capital purchases. Proposed base period: January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2027, with four (4) option years extending through December 31, 2031. SCOPE OF WORK Responding vendors must be capable of furnishing heavy equipment rental services on an as-needed basis, including delivery and pickup when requested by BEA. The rental fleet should encompass the following representative, non-limiting categories typically required by BEA, including but not limited to: � Rollers 79-in. & 84-in. double-drum; 84-in. padfoot 12-16 ton class; 84-in. smooth 13-17 ton class; 68-in. pneumatic 14 � 16 ton class � Soil compactors (Heavy-duty, suitable for earthwork and compaction operations.) � Dozers Medium-class with low ground pressure; Medium-class high-track configuration; Large-Class; Extra-large-class � Motor graders Heavy-duty suitable for road construction, maintenance & finish grading) � Excavators and attachments Hydraulic excavators including long-reach 35-ton to 40 ton class, 74-ton class, 90-ton class; Hydraulic Hammer attachments compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator, or 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator; Rotary cutters compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator; Multi-processor attachment compatible with 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator � Scrapers Heavy-duty self propelled and/or tandem-engine scraper suitable for large-scale earthmoving operations. � Articulated haul trucks (30-ton payload and/or 45-ton payload capacity) � Wheel loaders (Medium-production and/or large-or extra-large production) Fork attachment compatible with the proposed wheel loader; approx. 72-in and 96-in fork lengths � Water equipment (12K gal. watertower, water trucks with 6K gal. and/or 8K gal.) � Rubber track dump trucks (suitable for operation on soft ground or uneven terrain) Equipment furnished shall meet or exceed OSHA, ANSI, and applicable manufacturer maintenance standards; be delivered in safe, good working condition; and include required documentation (inspection records, manuals, tags, capacity charts). PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest submitted to chase.egbert@Inl.gov by close-of business on 02 Oct. 2026. Responses must include sufficient written information confirming the responder�s qualifications and interest. Company name and point of contact. NAICS and business size classification Description of rental fleet and capability to supply equipment in the categories listed above, including typical makes/models and availability windows. Delivery and pickup capabilities for INL locations; standard lead times; emergency response capability. Standard equipment delivery timelines should not exceed one-week from the date of request. Repair or replacement of malfunctioning or defective equipment should occur within 24-hours of notification. Maintenance, inspection, and documentation practices; sample service/inspection records. Repair and replacement response commitments (e.g., 24-hour repair/replace) and onsite service coverage. Safety, security, and compliance: confirmation of OSHA/ANSI compliance; onsite requirements (REAL ID; Foreign National Access Program approvals when applicable; BEA escort compliance). Quality program certifications and applicable regulatory compliance (e.g., DOT for transport). Standard rental terms (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) and pricing structures; discount schedules or IDIQ approaches (note: detailed pricing may be requested in a subsequent RFP). References for similar heavy equipment rental support to government or industrial sites. Note that responses must be no more than fifteen (15) pages in length in PDF format. Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

description: Introduction/Background The U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center (DEVCOM AC) Munitions Engineering Technology Center (METC), Medium and Cannon Caliber Munitions Division FCDD-ACM-MJ at Picatinny Arsenal, NJ is issuing this sources sought notice to conduct market research to determine the ability to perform complete life cycle engineering for a wide variety of munition systems across DEVCOM AC for various customers. This includes exploratory, advanced and engineering development, experimental testing, quality engineering, evaluation and qualification of munition systems and component concepts, as well as production and manufacturing engineering for munition systems and components. 2.Disclaimer THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. The Contractor shall apply engineering competencies to solve complex technical challenges throughout the munition system lifecycle by executing rigorous engineering activities. The Contractor shall apply core engineering disciplines by executing critical technical activities such as performing requirements decomposition and system architecture design; creating detailed Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models; conducting structural, thermal, and kinematic finite element analysis (FEA); designing analog and digital circuit boards; developing embedded software and control algorithms; and formulating developmental test plans alongside post-test data reduction. Through these tasks, the Contractor shall deliver engineering artifacts such as Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Technical Data Packages (TDPs), simulation reports, and software version descriptions and actively participate in formal/informal reviews to ensure robust engineering rigor, standard methodologies, and scientific discipline are applied to the development, production, and sustainment of the munition systems. They will review designs and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) against military and commercial specifications, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) standards, and producibility standards and proactively identifying opportunities to reduce costs, accelerate schedules, optimize manufacturing processes, and elevate overall quality. Throughout the life cycle, the contractor shall be responsible for supporting project preparation encompassing planning, cost analysis, scheduling, facility coordination, and integration. Finally, they shall be responsible for collaborating with multi-disciplinary program teams to support the reliable delivery and sustained performance of munition systems, aligning all efforts with operational utility and organizational mission requirements. 3.2 The individuals are expected to travel on a semi-regular basis. 3.3 The Contractor shall attend, support, and report on meetings, review documents, contribute to the preparation of original documents, analyze cost, performance, risk, and provide recommendations or courses of action and ensure objectives are met. 3.4 The Contractor shall support the generation and review of briefing materials. 3.5 The Contractor shall support, coordinate, participate, and record regular Integrated Product Team (IPT) meetings on assigned projects/programs. 3.6 The Contractor shall provide technical advice regarding project feasibility, definitions of project scope, complexities/risk involved, phases required, and time schedules. 3.7 The Contractor shall keep project team leads/ Armaments Project Officer (APO) and Branch and Division supervisors informed of program/project status, issues, problems and recommendations through oral communication, proper documentation including trip reports and attendance at regularly scheduled and informal meetings. Provide technical support and advice to project team leads/APOs and Branch and Division supervisors on engineering aspects of assigned munition systems. This shall include solution recommendations regarding major problems and conflicting requirements with assigned projects/programs. 4. title: Notice of Intent - BPA for Language Services
description: This Notice is not a call for sources, quotes, or solicitations. The deadline for response is 1700 EDT on October 3, 2026. Responses may be directed by e-mail to Angelika Graham, Contracting Officer, Office of Language Services, Department of State. Any technical or other information received in response to this Notice will be considered for the sole purpose of market research for future requirements. The Office of Language Services of the U.S. Department of State contracts directly with qualified individuals to provide foreign language interpreting, translating, and related services in support of diplomatic and foreign affairs activities at the highest levels of the U.S. Government. The Office has limited contracting authority pursuant to Department of State Acquisition Regulations (DOSAR), the Foreign Affairs Manual (FAM), and FAR Part 13 to contract for interpreters and translators domestically. DOSAR 601.601-70 further defines this as the authority �to enter into and administer simplified acquisition transactions under FAR Part 13 and orders against existing contracts up to the maximum ordering threshold or limitation for interpreting, translating, conference reporting, and related language support and escort services.� The Office establishes fixed rates of payment for specific language services each fiscal year on the basis of market research. In accordance with industry standards, these rates are not published for the general public. For the purposes of this Notice, the term �qualified� describes those individuals who have passed the Office of Language Services test(s) of interpreting and translating skill for one or more foreign languages and have successfully provided language services under a Blanket Purchase Agreement or Purchase Order with the Office of Language Services in the past. In accordance with 6 FAM 1550, the Office develops and administers examinations to evaluate the interpreting and translating skills of prospective direct-hire and contract staff. These exams are offered by invitation only subject to the needs of the Department. Individual members of the public who wish to be considered as test candidates should visit https://www.state.gov/freelance-linguists-ols/ to view criteria and application information. In addition, qualified bidders must hold U.S. citizenship or permanent resident status and have active contractor profiles in the System for Award Management (SAM). They must also be able to obtain and maintain a Moderate or High-risk Public Trust Certification from the State Department�s Office of Personnel Suitability and Security. They must agree to accept our fixed rates of payment for specific language services. Finally, they are forbidden from subcontracting and must adhere to strict professional standards. The Office of Language Services intends to issue Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for Language Services to qualified bidders effective October 1, 2026. The Office anticipates that roughly 850 Agreements with individual foreign language translators, interpreters, and specialists will be issued. The value of calls against these individual Agreements will not exceed $350,000, with no individual call to exceed $25,000 and over half of all calls at or below the micro purchase threshold $15,000. There is no guarantee of assignment under these Agreements. The anticipated total combined annual value of all calls against all of these Agreements is between $20 million and $30 million. Individual BPA calls are awarded at the discretion of the Language Services Contracting Officer, based on recommendations from Subject Matter Experts within the Office and factors including evaluated skill sets, prior performance, and availability to accept the assignment.
